items.title: NFL will not reach prediction market deals before the season starts and will not allow team-level deals, Front Office Sports reports via GambleRss
items.content_text: - **NFL will not reach prediction market deals before the season starts and will not allow team-level deals, Front Office Sports reports via GambleRss** — Front Office Sports reported the NFL has held talks with Kalshi, Polymarket and the CFTC but will have no prediction market deals in place when the regular season begins, and no team-level deals are currently allowed. items.content_text: - **CFTC asks Novig and ProphetX to delay listing micro sports contracts such as first-points scorer markets, SBC Americas reports** — SBC Americas reported the CFTC wrote to Novig and ProphetX asking the registered exchanges to delay listing some self-certified sports markets, citing concerns that micro event contracts such as which player scores the first points in a basketball game may not be allowed under the Commodity Exchange Act. items.title: Prediction markets beat polls on speed but not always on accuracy, election experts say at NEXTPredict panel
items.content_text: - **Prediction markets beat polls on speed but not always on accuracy, election experts say at NEXTPredict panel** — At the NEXTPredict Summit in New York on Friday, Columbia University professor Rajiv Sethi, Decision Desk HQ analyst Geoffrey Skelley and PredictIt CEO John Phillips, in a panel moderated by Chuck Todd, said prediction markets react to developments faster than polls and models but can react quickly and wrongly, citing the final 2024 Des Moines Register poll in Iowa. Sethi and Phillips chose prediction markets as their single forecasting method for the final week before the midterms, Skelley chose forecasting models, and Phillips said some of PredictIt's most active traders conduct their own private exit polls. ([NextPredict](https://nextpredict.io/market-news/industry/markets-beat-polls-speed-not-always-accuracy/))

items.title: Attorneys at NEXTPredict summit say state gaming laws should not apply to federally regulated event contracts as Supreme Court review looms, CDC Gaming reports
items.content_text: - **Attorneys at NEXTPredict summit say state gaming laws should not apply to federally regulated event contracts as Supreme Court review looms, CDC Gaming reports** — Panelists at the NEXTPredict Summit in New York on October 23, including Kalshi head of litigation Javalin Dedaj and Gemini Titan general counsel Brigitte Weyls, argued sports event contracts on federally regulated exchanges fall under the CFTC and should not be banned under state gaming laws. The panel followed split appeals rulings in the Third, Ninth and Sixth Circuits, with the New Jersey case now at the Supreme Court, Kalshi due to file its brief by November 9, and Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Elliot Stein expecting a Supreme Court decision in late 2027. ([CDC Gaming](https://cdcgaming.com/state-regulations-do-not-apply-to-federally-regulated-event-contracts-attorneys-say/))
